subject: Review requested: Free credit issuance pattern for NeonMetrics trial accounts
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] Self-serve credit cluster — NeonMetrics domain spikes

Hi team,

Observed a cluster of PLG signups this morning that were auto-granted free credits for NeonMetrics (company claim on signup). Quick summary: 
- ~28 accounts created between 08:30-09:05 PDT
- High similarity on device fingerprint (same UA + cookie patterns) and repeated disposable-email domains in the chain
- 22 of these accounts have unspent credits still active

I attached a CSV with the signup rows and a UA capture. Initial look points to either a partner-batched onboarding or a scripted signup farm. Can we triage and decide whether to pause further auto-issuance for NeonMetrics?

Attachments: signup_report.csv, ua_capture.txt

Thanks,
Aditya
Product Ops — Growth
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] Self-serve credit cluster — NeonMetrics domain spikes

Thanks for the flag, Aditya.

Marissa — can you run the quick checks (cookie/device hashes, IP entropy, duplication on signup tokens) and advise whether we should: 
1) Put NeonMetrics on manual approval for any further freecredit grants,
2) Revoke unspent credits issued in the last 24h, and/or
3) Reach out to the NeonMetrics contact to confirm legitimate batch onboarding?

If it looks like fraud, hold everything and escalate to Risk. If it looks like a legitimate partner flow, we should whitelist the corporate domain but only after verification.

I'm looping you both to keep this in David's inbox for tracking.

-David
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] Self-serve credit cluster — NeonMetrics domain spikes

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 09:45 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa — can you run the quick checks...

Done a first-pass. Key findings below (details in attached PDF):
- 24 accounts share identical device fingerprint hash and two identical IP /24 blocks (likely same set of machines behind NAT or a cloud VM cluster).
- 19 accounts used emails on disposable subdomains (e.g., neon-ops@tempmail[.]site). Two accounts used alice@neonmetrics.com and bob@neonmetrics.com.
- Token replay detected: same signup token value reused 6x within a 4-minute window.
- No matching billing information on file for any account (all self-serve).

Recommended immediate actions: 
- Pause auto-issuance for any NeonMetrics-related signups until verification (manual approval gate).
- Revoke unspent credits on accounts that failed device/IP entropy checks (22 accounts).
- Send verification request to the neonmetrics corporate contact asking for a list of team members and the intended billing email for production rollout.
- Create a HubSpot task and short form for partner verification to standardize this flow (linked).

I'll attach the evidence pack (fraud_evidence.pdf) and open FRAUD-4321 in Jira. If you want, I can draft the external message.

Marissa Cole
Growth Risk Analyst
Redwood Inference
Attachments: fraud_evidence.pdf
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wang <alice@neonmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Action required: verification for NeonMetrics trial credits

Hi Alice — I manage trial operations here at Redwood. We noticed a cluster of recent trial signups claiming association with NeonMetrics that triggered our automated fraud heuristics. Before we can allow more self-serve credits or re-enable auto-issuance for your team, we need quick verification: 

Please reply with the following by EOD so we can unblock you: 
- Confirmation that NeonMetrics (neonmetrics.com) authorized these signups,
- A short list of team members (name + corporate email) who should receive trial credits,
- The billing contact email you plan to use if you convert to paid, and
- Any partner or onboarding partner who may have done bulk imports.

We're happy to hold a 15-minute call to verify if that's easier. We temporarily paused auto-grants for NeonMetrics pending your response; all currently-issued credits are still valid but we have flagged the unverified accounts for review.

If you believe this is an error, please include logs/notes from your side that show those signups were legitimate.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Wang <alice@neonmetrics.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: support@neonmetrics.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action required: verification for NeonMetrics trial credits

David — thanks for the heads up and for the clear list. We spotted the same unusual activity on our end this morning — several signups showing as internal trials that we did not create. We're investigating with our IT team.

Quick answers: 
- NeonMetrics (neonmetrics.com) did not perform a bulk import this morning.
- I can provide a canonical team list (name + email) by EOD — sharing internally now.
- Billing contact is billing@neonmetrics.com.
- We don't have any partner onboarding running.

We appreciate the temporary hold — we do need credits for a product demo to a potential customer next week. If you can fast-track a manual verification (15-min call), that would help.

I'll send the team list and any logs we find in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Alice Wang
